name: Angles & Shapes
lesson: Angles on a straight line add to $180^\circ$, and angles around a point add to $360^\circ$.
The interior angles of a triangle add to $180^\circ$. An isosceles triangle has two equal angles opposite its equal sides.
A polygon can be split into triangles by drawing diagonals from one vertex. Count the triangles to find the polygon's angle sum.

problems.q: Two adjacent angles form a straight angle. One measures $118^\circ$. Find $x$.
problems.imageAlt: A straight line split by a ray into an angle labelled 118 degrees and an angle labelled x.

problems.q: A triangle has two angles measuring $48^\circ$ and $67^\circ$. Find its third angle.
problems.hint: Use the angle sum of a triangle.
problems.imageAlt: Triangle with two base angles labelled 48 degrees and 67 degrees, and the third labelled x.

problems.q: One acute angle of a right triangle measures $34^\circ$. What is its other acute angle?
problems.hint: The two acute angles add to $90^\circ$.

problems.q: An isosceles triangle has a $40^\circ$ angle between its equal sides. What is each of its other angles?
problems.hint: Share the remaining angle sum equally.
problems.solution: The remaining sum is $180^\circ-40^\circ=140^\circ$. Each equal angle is $70^\circ$.
problems.imageAlt: An isosceles triangle with matching ticks on its two equal sides and an apex angle labelled 40 degrees.

problems.q: Three angles of a quadrilateral measure $90^\circ$, $85^\circ$ and $110^\circ$. What is the fourth angle?
problems.hint: A quadrilateral can be split into two triangles.
problems.solution: Its angle sum is $360^\circ$. The fourth angle is $360^\circ-90^\circ-85^\circ-110^\circ=75^\circ$.

problems.q: One side of an equilateral triangle is extended. What is the exterior angle marked $x$?
problems.solution: The interior angle and $x$ make a straight angle, so $x=180^\circ-60^\circ=120^\circ$.
problems.imageAlt: An equilateral triangle with its base extended to the right; x marks the exterior angle.

problems.q: Three angles around a point measure $90^\circ$, $125^\circ$ and $x$. Find $x$.
problems.hint: All three make one full turn.

problems.q: A robot makes four equal turns in the same direction and completes exactly one full turn. How large is each turn?
problems.hint: Divide a full turn into four parts.

problems.q: A pentagon is split into three triangles by diagonals from one vertex. What is the sum of its interior angles?
problems.hint: Add the angle sums of the three triangles.
problems.imageAlt: A convex pentagon partitioned into three triangles by two diagonals from one vertex.

problems.q: A hexagon can be split into four triangles. All six interior angles of a regular hexagon are equal. What is each angle?
problems.hint: Find the total angle sum, then divide by 6.
problems.solution: The sum is $4\times180^\circ=720^\circ$. Each of the six equal angles is $720^\circ\div6=120^\circ$.

problems.q: A triangle's angles are in the ratio $1:2:3$. What is the largest angle?
problems.hint: There are six equal parts in the angle sum.
problems.solution: Each part is $180^\circ\div6=30^\circ$. The largest angle has three parts, so it is $90^\circ$.

problems.q: In an isosceles triangle, extend a side beyond the vertex where the equal sides meet. The exterior angle there is $112^\circ$. What is each base angle?
problems.hint: First find the interior angle at the vertex.
problems.solution: The vertex angle is $180^\circ-112^\circ=68^\circ$. Each base angle is $(180^\circ-68^\circ)\div2=56^\circ$.
